facts.statement: The holotype specimen UMNH VP 20205 was discovered by Donald D. DeBlieux in 2005 in the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah.
facts.quote: The holotype of Iguanacolossus, UMNH VP 20205, was discovered by Donald D. DeBlieux in 2005, unearthed from the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, Utah

facts.statement: Iguanacolossus was formally named and described in 2010 by a team including Andrew T. McDonald, James I. Kirkland, and Donald D. DeBlieux.
facts.quote: it wasn't named and described until 2010 by Andrew T. McDonald, James I. Kirkland, Donald D. DeBlieux, Scott K. Madsen, Jennifer Cavin, Andrew R. C. Milner, and Lukas Panzarin

facts.statement: The genus name Iguanacolossus combines the word for the modern reptile Iguana with the Latin word for giant, referencing its large body size and iguana-like teeth.
facts.quote: The generic name, Iguanacolossus, is a combination of the reptile genus "Iguana", and the Latin word "colossus" (meaning colossal and/or giant) in relation to the iconic Iguana-like teeth of iguanodontians and the notorious large body size of the specimen.

facts.statement: The specific name fortis means mighty.
Iguanacolossus was a large, robust dinosaur estimated to reach 9 meters in length and weigh 5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Iguanacolossus is a large, robust iguanodontid, probably reaching 9 m long and weighing 5 t in body mass.

facts.statement: The right pubis of Iguanacolossus displays both derived and primitive features found in related iguanodontians.
facts.quote: The right pubis shows derived and plesiomorphic features, seen on related iguanodontians.

facts.statement: Iguanacolossus is classified within the Iguanodontia, specifically as a styracosternan, a basal subgroup that includes Hadrosauridae and dinosaurs closer to hadrosaurs than to camptosaurs.
facts.quote: Iguanacolossus was placed in the Iguanodontia, being a styracosternan, a basal subgroup containing the Hadrosauridae and all dinosaurs more closely related to hadrosaurids than to camptosaurids.

facts.statement: Iguanacolossus lived approximately 130 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian stage) in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace unos 130 millones de años en el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Iguanacolossus is estimated from 139.1 to 132.6 million years ago, spanning the Berriasian to Valanginian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (139.1 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Iguanacolossus lived alongside theropods like Falcarius and Geminiraptor, the sauropod Mierasaurus, and the turtle Naomichelys in the Lower Yellow Cat bed.
facts.quote: Iguanacolossus was unearthed from the Lower bed, where it shared its environment with the theropods Falcarius, Geminiraptor and Yurgovuchia, the sauropod Mierasaurus and the turtle Naomichelys.

facts.statement: Indeterminate goniopholidids are known from the same Lower Yellow Cat environment as Iguanacolossus.
facts.quote: There are also indeterminate goniopholidids known from the Lower Yellow Cat.

facts.statement: Additional juvenile remains, including lower jaws and humeri, found at the Doelling's Bowl site are currently under revision.
facts.quote: Additional findings at the Doelling's Bowl site are currently on revision, compromising mostly juvenile material based on lower jaws and humerus.

facts.statement: The preserved maxilla of Iguanacolossus has 14 alveoli, suggesting an elliptical and elongate antorbital fossa.
facts.quote: The maxilla preserves 14 alveoli, the presence of two concave surfaces suggest an elliptical and elongate antorbital fossa.

facts.statement: The two right metatarsals of Iguanacolossus are identified as metatarsals III and IV based on comparisons with Camptosaurus and Iguanodon.
facts.quote: The two right metatarsals are classified as metatarsals III and IV based on Camptosaurus and Iguanodon.

rejected.statement: Iguanacolossus is a genus of large, robust iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Iguanacolossus (meaning "iguana colossus" or "colossal iguana") is a genus of iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period.
